problem_type: A paid canvas submit that is still in flight is forgotten when the project canvas is reloaded, so the node is offered for generation again and the provider receives a second paid request.
symptom: Canvas single-node generation: while the request has not come back, go to the project library and back. The node shows idle (image node, enter a prompt) and the bottom bar offers 'Generate all 1'; clicking it sends a second POST to the provider and the node later shows two versions (real app with loopback fixture: provider POSTs 1 -> 2).
direct_cause: Reopening the project restores the canvas from disk through normalizeStoreSnapshot; convergeStuckMidFlightNode treats every node persisted as running or queued without a provider task id as a ghost spinner left by a dead process and resets it to idle with its run cancelled. In a project switch the process is alive and the submit is still awaiting nomi:tasks:run, so the node becomes eligible in eligibleGenerationNodeIds (idle or error) and 'Generate all' submits again. Main had no per-node guard: nomi:tasks:run only deduplicates the same idempotency key, and a new click mints a new key.
class_root: 'Does this node have a paid submit in flight' had no owner that outlives a project-session release: the renderer derived it from persisted node status (project-scoped, collected on load) and the paid-submit boundary in main never checked it. The invariant: while a submit for a node is in flight, the node is shown generating, is not offered for generation, and the paid boundary refuses a second submit for that node, regardless of project switches.
affected_population: Every canvas single-node or batch generation going through nomi:tasks:run whose submit is still in flight when the user leaves the project and comes back
Synchronous providers are most exposed (no task id until the request returns); asynchronous providers are exposed until their create call returns
Present in v0.22.5 (same convergeStuckMidFlightNode and eligibility rule, no main guard)
entry_points: nomi:tasks:run (main paid-submit IPC boundary for all canvas runners)
runWorkbenchTaskByVendor (the renderer's only caller of tasks:run)
normalizeStoreSnapshot -> convergeStuckMidFlightNode (project open, external graph apply)
internal_only_reason: The invariant is about Nomi's own submit lifecycle across its own project-session release; no third-party API decides it.
invariants: Main refuses a nomi:tasks:run for (projectId, nodeId) while another one for the same node has not returned, with structured code node_generation_in_flight; idempotent replays of the same submit are merged before the guard.
The renderer records every submit it has awaiting tasks:run by node id, for the lifetime of the window process, not of the project session.
Loading a canvas never collects a running or queued node whose submit is still in flight in this window; it stays generating and therefore out of eligibleGenerationNodeIds.
The refusal is shown as 'still generating, this one was not sent' (i18n zh and en), not as a provider failure.

door_reduction.why_not: No door was merged: the fix adds the missing in-flight record (one writer in each process: trackNodeSubmit at the renderer's only tasks:run caller, withNodeSubmitExclusive at main's tasks:run boundary) and one reader in the load convergence. eligibleGenerationNodeIds keeps its two callers (batch dock and frame actions) because it already excludes running nodes; it needed no change once the load convergence stopped resetting in-flight nodes.

generality_proof: Every canvas runner reaches the provider through nomi:tasks:run, and the renderer reaches it only through runWorkbenchTaskByVendor, so both in-flight records sit on the single submit path. Every way a node can be offered again after a reload goes through convergeStuckMidFlightNode (the only place that turns a persisted running node idle) followed by the status-based eligibility rule, which now sees the node as running. Any other entry that still submits (a stale UI, an agent, a future button) is refused at the main boundary before a provider call.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: One paid submit in flight per (project, canvas node) at the main IPC boundary; refuses the second with a structured, truthful code.
Window-process record of submits awaiting tasks:run, read by the load convergence so a project switch does not collect a live run.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Excludes non-idle/error nodes; with the in-flight node kept running after load it no longer counts it (nodeSubmitInFlight.test.ts reported case).
Skips nodes with a submit in flight in this window; after a restart the record is empty and the ghost spinner is still collected (class test).
Wraps runTask in withNodeSubmitExclusive inside runTaskWithIdempotency (taskIpcHandlers.test.ts).
Runs the variants of one node strictly one after another (await per variant), so the per-node guard never refuses them.

recurrence.reason: Any canvas generation that is in flight during a project switch can be resubmitted by the user or by any other entry; the same reload path also runs when an external graph is applied.
same_class_scan: git grep 'tasks.run(' src: runWorkbenchTaskByVendor is the only renderer caller of nomi:tasks:run.
canvasProductionScope.eligibleGenerationNodeIds is the single status rule for batch generation (idle or error only).
git show v0.22.5:src/workbench/generationCanvas/store/canvasSnapshotNormalizer.ts: identical convergeStuckMidFlightNode; git show v0.22.5:electron/tasks/taskIpcHandlers.ts: no per-node guard.

Real app before the fix (canvas-switch walk with DOUBLE=1): after switching back the node is idle, 'Generate all 1' is offered, one click raises provider POSTs from 1 to 2 and the node ends with two versions.

prevention.invariant: At most one paid submit per (project, canvas node) is in flight, and the canvas keeps showing it as generating across project switches.
prevention.failure_mode: A second submit is refused before any provider call with code node_generation_in_flight and a zh/en message that this request was not sent.
prevention.strategy: Guard the shared paid-submit IPC boundary in main and give the renderer's load convergence a process-lifetime record of its own outstanding submits.

legacy_paths.rationale: No old path existed for this record; the load convergence keeps its restart behaviour and only stops collecting runs that are provably alive in this window.

migration: No data migration: both records live in memory only. After a restart nothing is in flight, so persisted spinners are collected exactly as before.

invariant_owner_layer.rationale: The paid-submit IPC boundary in main owns 'one submit per node in flight' (it is where money is spent and it outlives renderer project sessions); the renderer record is the window's own record of the same outstanding IPC calls, used only so the load convergence tells the truth.

residual_risks: After a renderer reload (not a project switch) while main still holds a submit, the node is collected to idle again; the main guard still refuses a second submit, but the node does not say 'generating' until the first returns.

Asynchronous providers: once the create call returns, the node carries a task id and follows the existing recoverable path; a deliberate rerun after that point is a new paid task and is not covered by this per-node guard.
Not run on a v0.22.5 build; the 0.22.5 conclusion is from reading its code.
